body.p: Claims 1-22 are pending. Claims 1, 8, 9, 11, 19, and 20 are amended. No new matter has been added.
Claims 1-22 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. §102(a)(1) as being anticipated by Taylor et al. (US Pre-Grant Publication 2019/0392641 Al) ("Taylor"). This rejection is respectfully traversed.

It has not been shown that Taylor discloses the recitations of claim 1. For example, it has not been shown that Taylor discloses "rendering a virtual object having the type of material in a virtual environment; and providing the set of audio data to be output as sound when the virtual object interacts with another virtual object in the virtual environment", as is recited in claim 1. Rather, Taylor describes emulating a sound of interaction of a first real- world object with a material of a second real-world object when a virtual object interacts with the second real-world object (see paragraph 60, "[t]raining data may be used initially to model input objects, positions from interactions, and strengths of interactions. As an example, a tester may bounce real world objects later to be emulated by virtual objects off certain known materials to record the initial sound profiles, which are associated with the known materials in a data structure"). As such, it has not been shown that Taylor discloses "rendering a virtual object having the type of material in a virtual environment; and providing the set of audio data to be output as sound when the virtual object interacts with another virtual object in the virtual environment", as is recited in claim 1. Hence, for the reasons set forth above, claim 1 is submitted to be novel in view of Taylor.
Moreover, for the same reasons set forth above, independent claims 11 and 20 are

submitted to be novel in view of Taylor. For example, for the same reasons set forth above, it has not been shown that Taylor discloses "a processor configured to . . . render a virtual object having the type of material in a virtual environment; and provide the set of audio data to be output as sound when the virtual object interacts with another virtual object in the virtual environment", as is recited in claim 11. As another example, for the same reasons set forth above, it has not been shown that Taylor discloses "the server configured to: . . . render a virtual object having the type of material in a virtual environment; and provide the set of audio data to be output as sound when the virtual object interacts with another virtual object
in the virtual environment", as is recited in claim 20. Hence, for the reasons set forth above, claims 11 and 20 are submitted to be novel in view of Taylor.
Claims 2-10 depend from independent claim 1, claims 12-19 depend from

independent claim 11, and claims 21-22 depend from independent claim 20. Hence, for the same reasons set forth above with respect to independent claims 1, 11, and 17, the dependent claims 2-10, 12-19, and 21-22 are submitted to be novel in view of Taylor.
Thus, it is respectfully requested that the section 102 rejection of claims 1-22 be withdrawn.
A Notice of Allowance is respectfully requested.
